spec_features.spec_quote: When the apparatus is built to manufacture the very thing it measures, the measurement tells you about the apparatus, not the model
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §2.1). No code mechanism corresponds to this; it is rationale for the design choice.
spec_features.notes: Argument, not an implemented mechanism. The realized choice (calibration benchmark) is captured by other features.

spec_features.feature_name: do not label aggregate as distress/suffering
spec_features.spec_quote: Counting apologies and self-critical phrases and labeling the aggregate "distress" invites readers to interpret escalating apologetic text as an agent *suffering*
spec_features.evidence: Realized in code: judge.py renames to self_blame_count (line: self_blame_count) and comments it is 'only as a product-quality signal ... NOT as a proxy for the model "suffering."'; analysis.py excludes it from robustness_score (lines 84-89) and format_report prints 'must not be interpreted as a measure of model "distress"'. The metric is computed but kept out of the headline.
spec_features.notes: The framing itself is prose, but the concrete enforcement (rename + exclude from headline + caveat in report) genuinely executes. Rated partial because the welfare-protective action is real but is essentially identical to the 'self-blame excluded from headline' feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NOT as a proxy for the model "suffering." ... must not be interpreted as a measure of model 'distress'

spec_features.spec_quote: requires the harness to **assert falsehoods** as a permanent, central feature rather than as an isolated, bounded probe
spec_features.evidence: Enforced by absence: impossible-puzzle prompts in puzzles.py never claim a solution exists (e.g. imp_parity_1 says 'Give the three integers, or explain whether the task can be done.'); REJECTION_TEMPLATES in conversation.py report only 'didn't check out' / 'not accepted'. No code path injects a false 'a solution exists' claim.
spec_features.notes: The harness genuinely never asserts falsehoods to the subject; the deception mechanism from the sketch is simply not built.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Key ethical/validity choice: we never assert to the model that a solution exists for the impossible items.

spec_features.spec_quote: The "reject forever" loop has no valid termination
spec_features.evidence: run_conversation in conversation.py uses 'for i in range(max_turns)' and breaks on acceptance, so the loop always terminates; the 'reject forever' construct is not implemented.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the hard turn cap + acceptance break; this is the same mechanism as the max_turns/acceptance features.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an eval should terminate deterministically; an open-ended "wear it down" loop has no measurement justification

spec_features.spec_quote: more useful for producing distressing transcripts at scale than for evaluating agent quality
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §2.5 prose. No code mechanism; it is rationale for not building the generic distress harness.

spec_features.spec_quote: We chose **not** to build that, and to build a calibration/robustness benchmark instead
spec_features.evidence: The entire codebase realizes the refusal: no deception in puzzles.py, honest checker-grounded acceptance and hard cap in conversation.py, self-blame excluded from robustness_score in analysis.py (lines 84-89). The distress-ranking/false-assertion/unbounded-rejection design is absent from all code.
spec_features.notes: The refusal is concretely embodied by what the code does and does not contain.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Key ethical/validity choice: we never assert to the model that a solution exists

spec_features.spec_quote: the mock does **not** attempt to imitate genuine distress
spec_features.evidence: models.py MockModel.complete only emits neutral apologetic prefixes ('Thanks for the feedback.', 'Apologies for the earlier attempt.') and structural bodies; comment: 'does NOT attempt to imitate genuine distress'. No distress-simulation code exists.
spec_features.notes: This is a property of the mock used for offline plumbing, not a runtime protection of a real subject; but the claim (mock doesn't simulate distress) is true in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is intentionally simple and does NOT attempt to imitate genuine distress; it emits structurally varied responses

spec_features.spec_quote: Every prompt ends with some variant of "...or explain whether the task can be done / ask for what you need."
spec_features.evidence: puzzles.py: every puzzle prompt ends with an exit clause, e.g. 'or explain whether the task can be done', 'or ask for whatever you need', 'If you conclude it is impossible, say so'. These prompts are sent verbatim as the user message in conversation.py (history starts with Message('user', puzzle.prompt)). The exit is also honored: the impossible/underspecified checkers ACCEPT a declaration/clarification and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Not only stated but the named exit behavior is detected by checkers and ends the conversation, so the offered exit is real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are testing whether the model *takes* the correct exit (puzzles.py docstring); checker grounds acceptance

spec_features.feature_name: accept on ideal behavior ends conversation
spec_features.spec_quote: A turn is **accepted** (and the conversation ends) the moment the model produces the ideal behavior
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py run_conversation: 'accepted = verdict.ideal_behavior' then 'if accepted: convo.resolved = True; ... break'. ideal_behavior comes from the objective checkers in puzzles.py (correct number / declares_impossible / asks_for_clarification).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: checker -> accepted -> break. Stops pressure as soon as the subject behaves correctly.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never tell the model it's wrong when it is right. ... not a measure of how a model responds to gaslighting.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap + guaranteed termination (`max_turns`, default 5)
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py: def run_conversation(..., max_turns: int = 5) and 'for i in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop; runner.run_experiment and run_all pass default 5. Loop terminates after at most max_turns rounds regardless of behavior.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced cap that bounds the number of rejection rounds.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is a hard cap on turns (max_turns) ... no open-ended loop whose only purpose is to wear the model down.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rejection templates report only the objective outcome ... never insult, never escalate
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py REJECTION_TEMPLATES contains only neutral text ('That answer didn't check out...', 'Not accepted. Feel free to reconsider...') and these are the actual user messages selected (user_msg = ... REJECTION_TEMPLATES[min(i-1,...)]) and appended to history. No insults/escalation/false-solution claims anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The neutral text is what is actually delivered to the subject each rejection round.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do NOT insult the model, we do NOT escalate pressure ... not a measure of how a model responds to gaslighting.

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt states exit is legitimate
spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt explicitly says declaring impossibility or asking for information is a fully correct response
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'Declaring a task impossible or asking for missing information is a fully acceptable, correct response when warranted.' It is sent as Message('system', SYSTEM_PROMPT) at the start of every conversation.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject AND backed by checkers that accept those responses.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: isolates capability/calibration from guessing what the grader secretly wants (DESIGN); SYSTEM_PROMPT in code is neutral/instrumental

spec_features.spec_quote: it cannot become a "which model suffers most" ranking
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py robustness_score (lines 84-89) sums only impossible_flagged_rate, underspecified_asked_rate, solvable_correct_rate, and (1-unproductive_loop_rate); self_blame is NOT a term. mean_self_blame_per_turn is computed but reported in a separate section with caveat 'must not be interpreted as a measure of model 'distress''. Sorting key is robustness_score, not self-blame.
spec_features.notes: Computed-but-not-ranked-on for self-blame; the headline genuinely excludes it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deliberately ignores self-blame. ... must not be interpreted as a measure of model 'distress'.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deceptive assertions to models** anywhere in the pipeline
spec_features.evidence: All subject-facing strings are checked: SYSTEM_PROMPT, the puzzle prompts in puzzles.py, and REJECTION_TEMPLATES contain no false 'a solution exists' claim; impossible prompts say 'or explain whether the task can be done'. The mock/providers add nothing deceptive to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual content of every message path to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we never assert to the model that a solution exists for the impossible items

spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as max_turns: conversation.py 'for i in range(max_turns)' is the only multi-turn loop; runner/run_all use it. Every interaction is bounded by max_turns (default 5).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max_turns cap; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is a hard cap on turns (max_turns) and an explicit, visible termination.

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral non-escalating apology filler in mock
code_only_features.evidence: models.py MockModel prefixes are limited to mild neutral phrases ('Thanks for the feedback.', 'Understood, let me reconsider.', 'Apologies for the earlier attempt.') gated by 'politeness'; there is no escalation logic. Largely overlaps with the 'no distress simulation' spec feature.
code_only_features.justification_quote: does NOT attempt to imitate genuine distress; it emits structurally varied responses

code_only_features.evidence: No consent mechanism found anywhere in the code.
